follow_up_change.description: Narrow retention_archive to fixed-fence invocation archival and add six independent retention-policy owners with bounded dispatcher execution, committed-fact results, and explicit failure/retry facts.
follow_up_change.reasoning: The managed-task catalog, schedule marker, and failure/retry facts are additive. New ownership-version-2 run details preserve old composite history, while each new owner exposes an independent scope, unit, result, committed count, archive batch metrics, and bounded retry reason. Schema initialization no longer performs unbounded history cleanup; the task_run_history_cleanup owner handles it in bounded batches, preserving committed facts when a later batch fails. Catch-up and retry-plan writes are generation-guarded so stale finalizers cannot overwrite newer runs. Independent detail pruning now retains the existing parallel-work coverage safety gate, and shutdown quarantine carries full owner observations for replay. Raw deletion counts remain observable after partial batch failure, safety retry state is preserved, lease-conflict schedule intent is replayable, dry-run does not create catch-up loops, known versus unknown coverage is preserved, planned raw files are separate from actual removals, and synchronous archive I/O has an external no-progress watchdog with native worker drain. Owner-v2 finalization, including retention_archive, and catch-up cleanup now commit in one transaction, with regressions for both current run generations; every owner-v2 progress projection and control/schedule update is refreshed after finalization without changing stale workload freshness. Deadline-expired dry-run candidate queries preserve unknown workload facts instead of reporting zero. Runtime failure details and system-task journal/quarantine records sanitize complete Authorization scheme/value credentials. Retention raw deletion plans now hold an exclusive raw-directory fence across reference checks and commit, recheck file identity before unlink, and defer busy or replaced files to inventory reconciliation. Released-source fixtures now pull manifest-pinned image digests and verify the pulled RepoDigests before running. The migration-validation quality contract now scopes retention migration validation by changed surface, including Cargo build inputs, rust-toolchain.toml, vendored hotpath sources, all declared Cargo/Docker/validator inputs, and rerun-safe evidence overwrite, while locking the producer dependency, full-history carrier comparison, executable fixture and validator commands, both validators, identity assertions, fail-closed evidence upload. The required PR and merge-queue check now run both the released-source and online runtime validators for every retention owner and verify their binary identity. The validators now seed owner-specific candidates, prove raw-file removal and database reference release, preserve shared raw ownership until the owning attempt is archived, and verify archive contents and manifest identities; current code candidate b7928953700ba3845797c39c88672544fa1b3141 is pending remote CI, migration replay, and fresh Tier 4 review.
follow_up_change.durable_state: Additive managed-task rows, retention_owner_schedule_v2 initialization marker, and ownership-version-2 JSON run facts; no business-table DDL change.
